input.title: Battery complaints in Premium Thin & Light: long-standing, intensified, and mixed evidence on battery-positioned products

claims.text: Premium Thin & Light has the highest recent battery complaint rate at 6.9% [6.7%, 7.1%], versus Budget 3.8%, Gaming 3.4% and Mainstream 3.4%.

In Premium Thin & Light the battery complaint rate moved from 4.4% to 6.9% (diff +2.5%, CI +2.2% to +2.8%), status intensified_long_standing, q_value_bh 0.0. Pooled segment rates can move with product mix, and complaint labels come from an unvalidated classifier.
Other segments show no material change: Budget +0.3% was labelled no_material_change, Gaming (q 0.1182) and Mainstream (q 0.9497) were not significant.

The battery complaint issue was already present in the 2021-M01..2022-M06 baseline (4.4% in Premium Thin & Light), so it is long-standing and has intensified rather than being new. Complaints are spread across 28 products, and the top product accounts for 12.6% of recent complaints.

Three Premium Thin & Light products were marketed on battery life. P0113 (Altura Aero 13 G4) was advertised as up to 20 hours, P0050 (Brevik Aero 14 G4) as up to 17 hours, and P0120 (Corvane Lumen 14 G2) as up to 18 hours alongside an OLED display. These are manufacturer claims, not real-world performance, and P0120's positioning is borderline.
Estimated first observed sale (an estimate, not a verified launch date) is 2023-M10 for P0113 and 2023-M11 for P0050, both usable. P0120's is unreliable (2022-M04), so it was not compared.

P0113 had a mean segment share of 18.09% over its first 12 months versus a cohort median of 3.88% (rank 1 of 15, q_value_bh 0.0074). Its battery complaint rate was 3.2% versus a cohort median of 9.0% (q_value_bh 0.0132). These are descriptive associations, not evidence that battery positioning caused them.

P0050 showed no detectable difference from its cohort. Its share was 5.66% versus a median of 3.88% (q 0.4675). It was 5.05% with the pattern months excluded (q 0.6397), and its battery complaint rate was 8.8% versus 8.7% (q 0.542). Samples are small, so this is not evidence of equivalence.
P0050 shows an observed price-and-volume pattern in 2024-M02 and 2024-M03 (max ASP drop -22.89%). The data contain no promotion records, so a promotion is not confirmed.
Rubric grades: segment signal Moderate; P0113 Moderate; P0050 Not supported; P0120 Insufficient.

P0113's outcomes could possibly reflect cohort composition (matched only on first-sale timing and early ASP; the cohort includes battery-positioned P0050), buyer mix, or comment propensity rather than battery positioning. A display placebo check showed no detectable difference for P0113 (2.5% vs 2.2% cohort median, q 0.6397), which does not support a general low-complaint pattern but does not rule out the alternatives.

Only two products could be tested and their results diverge. The windows (2023-M10 to 2024-M10) do not match the recent segment rise window (2024-M07 onward). The data have no distribution, availability or preference measures. The evidence is insufficient to say whether battery positioning worked or what happened to the segment complaints.

For analyst evaluation only: P0113's pairing of high segment share and low battery complaints may be worth investigating for factors beyond the battery claim (brand, hardware, channel). The evidence here does not establish that battery positioning is an opportunity.

follow_ups: Label the battery positioning of all cohort members and rebuild cohorts excluding other battery-positioned products.
Run sensitivity windows (6 and 9 months) for P0113 share.
Check product-level battery complaint trends over 2024-M07..2025-M12 to link to the segment rise.
Obtain a reliable entry date for P0120, then run launch and complaint comparisons.
Review firmware, hardware and brand data for P0113; seek distribution data if available.
